And the main task of that department was to maintain the equipment in the power plants, telecommunication systems, and we also managed the fleet of vehicles, and I worked for that company between 1998 and 1992 [As interpreted] on the tasks of security and planning for defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, just now I believe you said between 1998 and 1992. Did you mean 1988?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC
utterances.text: Sorry, it was 1988. I apologise. My mistake. 1988 and 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And then you worked there again after the war; correct?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. After the war, the company has been reduced, has shrunk, two electrical power plants were given to the Herceg-Bosna power management board. So the number of employees went down as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can you tell the Judge, please, what's the name of this company?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC
utterances.text: Its full name is Elektroprivreda of Bosnia-Herzegovina public company. And the part of the company that I work for is Hajdroelektrana [phoen] on the Neretva River.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Okay. So can the Judges understand that essentially this company, or at least the part of the company that you work for, is a hydroelectric generation company in the Jablanica area?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Idrizovic, during the time that you've been employed with this company, did you ever know a man by the name of Alojz Rados?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I knew Alojz Rados. I knew him then. I knew him before then as well, because we were neighbours. We lived next to each other in two adjoining buildings. Jablanica is a small place. It has about three -- 3500 inhabitants, so everybody knows everybody else. So I knew Alojz before that period and during that period.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Approximately how many years had you known Mr. Rados before the two of you worked at the company?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC
utterances.text: I had known him for at least ten years.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And did there come a time in early -- in the early 1990s, or previous to that if it was, that you and Mr. Rados both worked for this hydroelectric company in Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC
utterances.text: December 1988 until April 1992. During that time we worked in the general affairs department of this maintenance department.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: So you worked -- is it correct, sir, you worked in the same department of the same company?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Did you work -- two of you work in the same building?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, we worked in the same building.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can you give the Judges, please, an idea of how often in the course of your -- both of your employments at that company, how often in the course of your employment would you and Mr. Rados see each other?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC
utterances.text: We saw each other every day. We worked in the same building which we entered at the same time. We went to have lunch together. We would go back from lunch together. We would leave work together. So we saw each other every day more than once every day.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: During the time that you knew Mr. Rados at the company, did you have frequent occasion to see Mr. Rados's handwriting; for example, in company documents?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I saw it quite often. Rados was an officer in charge of protection against fire, and I was in charge of plans -- defence plans for the company.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can you give the Judges, please, some --

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I didn't finish. I wanted to say something else.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC
utterances.text: I apologise. I thought I should slow down because of the interpreters. Alojz would issue orders for protection equipment. So when he needed it, protection equipment, he would issue written orders, both for me and for my employees. And with these written orders, we would go to the warehouse of the company, from which we would get the protection clothing and equipment. So that was one of the tasks that he was charged with and the tasks in which we cooperated. He would do it in his own handwriting. He would fill out forms. And his other task was when I was drafting my defence plans, he would send me his proposals for fire protection because he was the one who was in charge of all the fire extinguishers and all the other equipment that served as protection against the gases in the boiler room, so all the equipment that was related to fires and protection against fires. So on my request, he would send me all that, so I would incorporate all that into my overall defence plan.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Is it correct, then, sir, that not only did you see documents written by Mr. Rados, but in the course of your own duties you relied on and used documents written by Mr. Rados?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. With regard to the aspect that I have mentioned, working out defence plans and working out a system of fire protection.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Now, we'll come back to those -- some of these things in a few minutes, sir. But now I want to direct your attention to the period of the war. During the war, in particular during 1992 and 1993, did you have occasion to see or know Mr. Rados during the war?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, very often.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Was he a member of the HVO in the Jablanica area?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Were you aware of any position or function that he held or performed in the HVO at that time?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was aware of his position. He was in charge of general affairs in the HVO staff. During one period I think he was responsible for information and propaganda. I think that was the field he dealt with.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Did you ever see him in meetings or gatherings of HVO officers or, in other words -- let me rephrase that, in meetings involving, say, both the HVO side and the ABiH side did you see Mr. Rados?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I did see him.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can you tell the Judge, please, whether you saw Mr. Rados performing or engaging in any particular function or activity during these meetings.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC
utterances.text: Well, in the course of the meetings -- well, for the most part he kept a record, his own record.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And how would he do that?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC
utterances.text: Sometimes he had official notebooks with him. Sometimes he would do it on pieces of paper, double-sided pieces of paper. It depended on the meeting. Sometimes they were party meetings. Sometimes they were military meetings. Sometimes it was a combination of the two. Sometimes it was at the War Presidency. It depended on the subject matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And he did this in longhand, in handwriting, sir?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If I can ask the usher to please show you Exhibit 258.2. Mr. President, I hope there is a bundle of exhibits that have been provided to the Chamber for this witness, as far as I know. I hope you have them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Defence counsel has not received any copy. That's why I'm asking. We haven't received those documents. Defence counsel hasn't received them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Then they should be -- I understood they had been distributed. Please can they be distributed. It's -- it's what you have in your hand, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, if you can direct your attention, please, to Exhibit 258.2, a document dated the 2nd of March, 1993 to the Presidency of the Jablanica HVO. Can I direct your attention to the very last sentence of that document. Does it say, sir: "For further clarification and cooperation, please contact the battalion administrative officer, Mr. A. Rados"?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. This confirms what I said a minute ago, that he was responsible for those general tasks, for general affairs. He was in charge of HVO administration.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. So based on your knowledge of Mr. Rados and the functions that you saw him performing during the war, including taking minutes at meetings, this would be consistent with the description of Exhibit 258.2; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, I now want to direct your attention --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, I hope the Chamber will recognise that I'm directing the witness to very narrow and specific topics for direct examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I'm now directing your specific attention, Mr. Idrizovic, to the end of July or the latter part of July 1993. Did you become aware at that time that there was fighting between the HVO and the ABiH in the area of Doljani?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I was very well aware of that fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: At the conclusion of that fighting, did the ABiH essentially re-take or re-gain the territory around Doljani from the HVO?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Towards the end of July, units of the 44th Mountain Brigade managed to take over a large part of Doljani.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can you tell the Judges, did it come to your attention that as part of that operation or at the conclusion of the fighting that various HVO documents and records were found or captured?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. About two days after part of Doljani had been taken over by the ABiH, I was told by a friend, a security officer in the brigade who used to be in the staff with me when the units were under my command, I was told that a large amount of documents had been seized and Rados Alojz's diary too, and Zajko, Alojz, and I worked in the same company. We were employed by the same company. He said Mr. Sihirlic told me that a large number of documents had been seized, including Alojz's private diary.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Did you understand or come to know where these documents had been seized, that is, sir, where were they physically located at the time they were collected by the ABiH?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Sihirlic told me that they had been found in their command in Doljani in Juric's house, which was next to a fish pond next to the Doljanka River. And further away behind there was a Catholic church. We knew that their command -- we already knew that their command was located in that house.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: When you say "the command" or "their command," whose command are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC
utterances.text: I'm referring to the HVO. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And when you say "Juric's house," what was located at Juric's house?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC
utterances.text: Well, the command was located there, the entire command. It was a battalion. It wasn't a very large unit. So there probably weren't very many people in that command, because in total they had about -- between 300 and 350 men.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: When you say, sir, there was a fish pond next to the Juric house, what do you mean by a fish pond?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC
utterances.text: How should I put it? There were concrete constructions there, concrete moulds, concrete beds in which -- which were supposed to contain fish.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And then at that location, according to what you know, sir, who collected -- what component or element of the ABiH forces collected the HVO documents that were found there?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC
utterances.text: Those documents were discovered by the military police because it is common practice everywhere that when entering such buildings, commands, and other important buildings, one might expect the area to be mined. So the police that has professionals at its disposal checks to see whether it's possible to enter such buildings safely. They checked the building. They established that it hadn't been mined. They found the documents there, collected the documents, and handed them over to the brigade supervisor.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, sir, you've already mentioned this in answering one of my previous questions. But so it's clear, among the documents that were found at that time, did those documents include what you've described as Mr. Rados's diary?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And can you tell the Judges, please, did you or members of your municipal staff become directly involved with that diary in some -- sometime soon after it was captured?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, we did. One evening Mr. Zajko -- I think that was on the 30th, and the shelling had stopped. It was in the late evening -- he came to my house. We're friends. He brought that diary because Alojz was a colleague of ours, and he said that there was something interesting that belonged to Alojz. He also brought a copy of the document with him, and he told me that in the brigade they had decided to copy the document and to provide the press with a copy so that the public could be made aware of its existence and so that our people and the family members of HVO soldiers who were in Jablanica could be informed of what was happening and be told who was attacking them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Around that time, sir, was a typed version of the diary prepared?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. In the command they decided - and it was no longer a problem then - they decided to copy it out, type it out, to make it easier for the press to read and to make it easier for it to be read in general for us who wanted to have copies. Our typists typed it out, and we then copied this version too, so anyone could have a copy of that diary. Our intention was to make this available to the largest possible number of people. That was in fact the only thing we read in 1993. We didn't have time for anything else.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Well, let me ask you to explain to the Judges why it is that there was such interest in this diary.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC
utterances.text: Well, after the 15th of April, the contents were very interesting. It was interesting because these people up there, they were all colleagues of ours. They were neighbours, friends from work. So it was interesting to see what our -- what these friends of ours had turned into.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, after the diary was typed, what happened to the diary after that?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC
utterances.text: After that, it remained in the brigade with the security organ right up until the end of war or rather up until the time when the brigade was disbanded, somewhere towards the end of 1996.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And did anything happen to it -- or who had it after the brigade disbanded?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC
utterances.text: Well, in the course of the war we'd formed a veteran's union and our intention was to retain memories of our fallen friends and to take care of their families and of their children. We wanted to try to do something to prevent people from forgetting what had happened at the time. In order to achieve this -- all the documents that could serve to help us document that four-year period, we collected all these documents in the veteran's union. And that also included the documents that we had confiscated from the HVO. These documents were important ones, and then there were other documents, documents from various other services, from the state organ services, the military hospital, the war hospital, the industrial facilities, documents relating to education, et cetera, et cetera. So the documents from various -- which had to do with various fields of life. We managed to do this, and the first thing that we did was to publish a book in which a list of the fallen soldiers had been compiled. I wanted to bring it with me, but I haven't. I'll do so tomorrow if I have the opportunity. In the future, if we get a sponsor, we'll also make a small book, several thousand copies, which will be a book of -- a book based on Alojz's diary and hand it out to people. One part of this union's volunteer work is to establish the chronology of all the events in the course of the war, which should be based on certain documents, which will be included in the book so that we can give some generations who did not participate in the war the possibility of being informed about this. We can be subjective, but this isn't a task for us. We need -- some time has to pass so that someone could examine this in an objective way. And in order for this to be examined objectively, it is necessary for a certain period of time to elapse, first of all.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, did there come a time when various of the documents that had been captured, the HVO documents, including the diary, did there come a time when some of those documents were turned over to somebody else?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC
utterances.text: Well, as it wasn't a secret, the fact that we had captured documents, and this diary had been published. It was on cable TV. It had been read out on several occasions. People had copies of this diary. It wasn't a secret and we didn't try to conceal this. This wasn't our intention, and there was no one we wanted to hide it from. We had no reason to hide it. We had good reason to publish it. And then people of ours from the AID probably discovered this through their lines. They came to Zajko and to me and asked us to provide them with copies of this diary and certain other documents because they needed them. As Zajko and I were members of the leadership in the veteran's union, they knew that too. There was no reason for us not to provide these people with the document because if the document remained in our hands, it wouldn't have much importance.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: When you say "Zajko," is that the first name of a man who you knew?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Zajko Sihirlic. He's the security officer from the brigade, a friend of mine. We continued working together in the community after the war. It's a non-governmental organisation. We work there as amateurs because we want to, as volunteers. We have no benefit. We don't benefit from this. But this is for the sake of our friends who died and for the sake of their children.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Was it you and Mr. Sihirlic who actually turned over the diary to the representative of AID?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, the two of us turned the document over.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And approximately, sir, as best you can, the year or however information -- however much information you can give us. Approximately when was it that this diary was turned over to AID?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC
utterances.text: 1997. But I couldn't be more precise. I can't remember. Many things passed through our heads at the time -- many things have passed through our heads, so it's difficult for me to remember events, to remember the dates.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Did you make a copy, sir, of the typed version of the diary before these documents were turned over to AID?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did. We did that immediately at the beginning of August 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can I ask the witness to please be shown Exhibit 928D. Now, Mr. President, at this time -- because there's going to be references to certain different, if you will, copies of versions of the diary, it occurred to me after this morning that it might be helpful to have kind of a list to keep it straight. So I'm going to provide to the Chamber, if I may, and to Defence counsel and others -- Madam Usher, if you could provide those, please, to -- one copy to the each of the Defence teams and a copy to the Judges, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, sir, do you have before you now what's been marked as Exhibit 928D?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And is that a copy -- is that the copy of the diary that you kept -- that you made and kept in 1993?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And has that document -- that copy, your copy of the document, continuously been in your possession since you first obtained it in 1993?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Could I next ask that the witness please be show 928B. I thought you had the whole bundle. Maybe it's already -- maybe he already has it. Sorry, Mr. President. Could I possibly see one of the bundles that were given to the registrar, please, to see if I can help straighten things out. It's a different bundle. It's not this bundle. It's the one that has this graph on the front.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I think we have the P928 -- P928A, B, C, under /5.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: That's fine. If you have -- excuse me, Mr. President. If you have 928B, that's what I'm referring your attention to, sorry, and to the witness. If the witness could be shown 928B, as in boy. It's not in that bundle. There's two bundles. One bundle has -- it looks like a graph sheet on the front. Mr. President, the page -- if you have this, the binder -- the separate bundle that has -- looks like a spreadsheet, if I can use that term, on the front. If you have that bundle -- it should have been marked, and my apology -- it should have been marked as 928B, but apparently by oversight it was not. There's a handwritten -- there's a typed version. You have a typed document and then you have starting on the numbered -- what we call the ERN number, 00799612. It's a handwritten -- it's a Xeroxed copy of a --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, we've found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Okay. If that could be shown to the witness, please, just that item.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, looking at 928B, sir, which is the document that's been placed in front of you, can you tell the Judges what that is?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC
utterances.text: A bad copy. And my sight is not so good.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Okay. It's a bad copy of what, sir?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC
utterances.text: My sight is not so good. The copy is bad.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If you can turn to the first few pages and look at the copy. Just open the first couple of pages and look at the document. Look what's in there.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC
utterances.text: So this is a bad copy of the title page of Alojz's diary.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And can you please now -- can the usher please show you -- and this will be not in the bundle but it will be -- 928C, which rather than use the term "original," I will currently just describe it as the blue-ink diary. Sir, I want you to open and look at the document -- the item that's been put in front of you marked 928C. Can you please tell the Judges, if you can, what that document is.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC
utterances.text: This is the diary that we're talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Is that a diary written in blue ink in a small -- what might be described as a journal? Is that the diary that was found and which you first saw in July 1993?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can you tell the Judges, please, so far as you know, from what you've been told and what you've already told us in fact, was that blue-ink diary, marked as 928C, one of the documents found at the fish farm?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'm just pausing because I'm just trying to keep -- that's exactly the reason I created this list, was to try to keep us as straight as possible. Let me ask -- Mr. President, I don't know if again you were given before -- and I apologise for these difficulties, but if you don't already have, could you be shown -- provided with 928D. I think, Mr. President, you'll told me a few moments ago that you had A, B, and C, but I'm not sure whether you said you have D.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we have D already, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Oh, very good. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, if you can assist us then, please. The blue-ink document was found in July 1993. Your municipal staff prepared a typed version of that document, still in the Serbo-Croatian language; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Later on this was typed all over the place, wherever there was a typewriter, wherever there were people who had time. Various people typed it, in the staff, in the command, wherever there were technical possibilities for typing it out.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And that's exactly, sir, why I asked you -- in terms of 928D, that is the copy of the typed diary that you personally kept and have had since 1993; correct?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Looking at the blue-ink diary, 928C, the book. If you could just open that for me, please, sir. Can you tell the Judges in looking at that document whether you recognise the handwriting?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Whose handwriting is it?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC
utterances.text: There has been some confusion. I said yes and then I didn't hear anything else. Did I answer your question, or did you ask me anything else?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: My apologies, sir. It didn't come through on the transcript. Perhaps it didn't -- wasn't picked up. Let me repeat my question. I asked if you recognised the handwriting, you said yes. And my question was: Whose handwriting is it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I've been quiet most of the time, but now I have to object for principle reasons. If a question like that was put, the usual answer was the witness is not an expert so you cannot ask him that. Can we please adhere to the same principles. The witness is not an expert, and this is not a question that he can answer. I am doing it for principle matters in order to behave in the same way across the board with the witnesses who are not experts on people's handwritings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I notice that you kept quiet the previous 30 minutes, but I hope you hear the testimony of this witness before. This witness told us that he was very familiar with the handwriting of that person and that they were in the same, you know, factory, and I think, you know, this question is allowed. Would you please repeat your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, can you tell the Judges whose handwriting that is.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC
utterances.text: This is Alojz Rados's handwriting.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And have you been able, sir, to obtain any prior records of the company that you both worked for that also bear Mr. Rados's handwriting?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can the witness please be shown Exhibit 68.4. It should be the top document on the bundle that looks like a spreadsheet. Nothing is going to be in that rebuttal exhibit binder. If you can put that aside, it might avoid confusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, can you describe to the Judges what kind of a document this is. Are you familiar with it? And just tell them what this document is.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I'm familiar with this document. This is a record of accidents and injuries that took place in 1990 in the department for maintenance. So this shows you a list of five workers who were injured that year, and Rados in his own handwriting filled out the form describing the incident, giving the date, the name of the injured person, and so on and so forth. He also signed this document, and everything is as clear as a bell.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Could I ask you -- sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Madam Usher, I'm going to need your assistance, please. If you could put that on the ELMO, that Exhibit 64. Could you -- could I ask that the witness be provided a marker.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And sir, can you find -- first of all, point out what you've just described a moment ago as the signature of Mr. Rados. Can you just point to that. You have to look -- I'm sorry, sir. You have to point -- can I ask you not to point at the screen.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC
utterances.text: I apologise. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: It's all right.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. If you could be provided a marker, sir. Will you circle that, please.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And would you just make a number "1" by that.

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And sir, is it correct then, based on what you've said, that the handwriting on this business record is the handwriting of Alojz Rados?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If -- Madam Usher, I think that's fine. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, if you have the blue-ink document in front of you, I think that's perhaps the easiest thing for you to work with, perhaps the most -- well, I'll leave it to you. But can I ask you to look, please, at pages -- using the pages of diary itself, of the original, can you find page 123.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And Mr. President, counsel, in the English translation, which is 928, the typed English translation, it begins on page 23.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: But if you can find page 123, sir. Do you have that?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I apologise. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Now, do you see an entry on that page that's dated the 18th of December, 1992?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. This was a meeting relative to a letter written by the HDZ to the SDA in which they informed them about the takeover of authorities and incorporating Jablanica into Herceg-Bosna. The meeting was initiated by the HDZ.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I -- Your Honours, I thought that my learned friend will abide by your ruling, and I believe that the contents of the diary are not the subject matter of the examination. Just the diary itself. I don't think that the contents of the diary should be the subject matter of the examination by the -- by my learned friend.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, if I am not mistaken, that during this meeting this witness personally participated in that meeting. We are not interested in what the meeting discussed. We're only interested whether this meeting is held at that time. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, that's exactly right, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, because of the constraints of time and possible objections by counsel, let me put the question to you this way: Have you had occasion before -- before this moment to look at the entry -- the full entry that goes on for several pages about this meeting on the 18th of December, 1992? Have you looked at that before?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. The minutes were taken of this meeting by both parties involved in it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. For the record, Mr. President, again, in terms of the typed English translation, I just simply refer the Chamber to -- and counsel to pages 23 through 31, and in the blue-ink diary pages 123 to 133.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, my question to you, sir, is: Based on your review of that entry for the 18th of December, 1992, does the information entered in Mr. Rados's diary accurately reflect what happened at that meeting?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I'm going to direct your attention to one other entry specifically.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, I think with some -- with a little bit of good luck, we can hopefully finish the direct examination before -- by the end of the day.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Could you please in a similar fashion find your way to --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: This isn't my day, Mr. President. It could be -- Mr. President, can I have the usher's assistance, please. If I can look at the exhibit for a moment. I think I wrote down the wrong page number.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I think I may have it. If you could direct your attention, sir, to page 147.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And Mr. President, the English translation, page 42.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, I'd like you, please, to just scan your eyes down page 147. And do you see another entry on that page which you believe is a reference to you?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. On this page, Mr. Rados says that a correct relationship is possible with Commander S.I. At that time the commander, whose initials were "S.I." was me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Safet Idrizovic?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, "S.I." stands for Safet Idrizovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, Mr. President, I'm come back -- I'm not going to do this in front of the witness. But if you look at -- well, I'll come back. There's some other information we'll come back to. Well, let me do this. I take that back.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, on the page that you're looking at in the original blue-ink document where it says "S.I." Is there anything in that document that says "Information and Security Service"? On that page 147, where you see the letters "S.I."

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Is there anything in the entry about you that talks about the Information and Security Service in that entry as to you?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC
utterances.text: It says here everybody is armed in the town. They produce G's, which stands for "grenades." But it seems these are being transported away immediately.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President -- that's fine, sir. You'll see, Mr. President, that he's gone down on the English translation on page 42, he's gone down and you'll see where he talks about that. I'll come back to it. I think on that point it's confusing. I think the documents will speak for themselves. If the witness could please direct your attention -- his attention to Exhibit 424.1, which is a separate document in that stack.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Meek.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Well, Mr. President, due to the Trial Chamber's overruling of Mr. Krsnik's last objection and due to the fact that the Prosecution is very eagerly wanting to get this witness home, I must object because this exhibit has nothing whatsoever to do with the diary and it's outside the scope of what the purview of the rebuttal evidence specifically -- what this witness would offer and by way of testimony by your ruling. For that reason, Your Honour, I object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we haven't found that document yet. Let me find it first. I don't know what kind of document it is at this moment. Mr. Scott, where could I find that document?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: In the -- I hope, Mr. President, that in the bundle where you've been looking at the documents you should have 424.1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, I -- Mr. President, I am finishing this witness. And as I said, I hope to be finished before 4.00. But among the documents, some of which are already admitted, and one or two that were not, this witness is in a position, because of his testimony -- the testimony he's already given, to identify documents that were found and some of the documents that he in fact initialled. And I simply want to take him through five documents and then my direct examination is finished.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Meek.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Mr. President, this witness wasn't here to identify other documents other than this alleged Rados diary. Why are you allowing the Prosecution to introduce -- you know, have this witness to talk about documents that have nothing to do with the diary? That's what the rebuttal evidence was for. That's what this witness was going to testify to, Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I haven't read this document yet. I just -- minutes, something like this. I think this document has been admitted into the evidence on the 4th of October of this year. But we'll see, you know, where -- how the Prosecution is going to use this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, if you have 424.1 -- not in the documents, not in the diary. You have the 424.1 document. Do you recognise the handwriting on that document, sir?

utterances.speaker: SAFET IDRIZOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. This is obviously Alojz Rados's handwriting. His signature is so distinct that it is not easily mistaken for anybody else's, and he also has a very distinct handwriting, very precise, very clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And if I could have the usher's assistance, I'm going to direct your attention -- I'm going to attempt to direct your attention very quickly to 318.1, 368, 389, and 418.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Just for clarification, have these been admitted? All four or any of these four that Mr. Scott just mentioned, if he can tell me if they've been admitted, I'd appreciate it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sure. Just let me -- give me a minute. 318 -- excuse me, 318.1 has not yet been admitted. 368 is admitted. 389 is admitted. And 418 I'm told is also admitted. Mr. President, if they're admitted, I won't go into them. I think the witness could assist the Chamber, but I won't go into them if the Court doesn't want me to. I will ask him -- I would like to ask him about 318.1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Scott, I have to advise you that at most we could sit at quarter past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: This is my last question. If he can look at 318.1.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, can you tell the Chamber whether that was one of the documents found at the fish farm in July 1993. And I'll ask you -- I'll ask you in a moment how you know that, but can you -- first of all, can you tell the Judges whether that was a document found at the fish farm.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Meek.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: I'm not objecting because it's his last question. I'm objecting because this has nothing whatsoever to do with the diary. This witness was here to testify about the alleged diary. We've gone beyond that, and now he wants to talk about documents that were purportedly found -- this witness wasn't even there by the way -- in Doljani in July of 1993. It's well outside the scope, Your Honours. Please, I object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, as for the last document, you know, at first I think it has nothing to do with the diary, but it turned out to be a minute written by Mr. Rados. But I'm not sure, you know -- at this moment I don't know what's the relationship of this document with the diary. Maybe Mr. Scott could show us about that so we could have a clear idea.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, I've always tried to be extremely -- completely transparent with the Chamber. This document is not related to the diary, but the -- this witness was simply in a position to be able to testify -- it has his signature and date on it, and it was turned over, and that he could authenticate it as one of the documents found at the fish farm. I thought it would assist the Chamber. If we're playing by these hypertechnical rules, I'll certainly abide by the Chamber's ruling.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Then again, Mr. President, if it please the Trial Chamber, my objection stands. The Prosecutor has agreed that this is outside the scope of what this Trial Chamber ordered on rebuttal evidence. But we're in your hands, Your Honour. If the rules want to change once again, then so be it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Scott, I still do not see your point.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: The point is simply to authenticate it as a document the Prosecution was previously offered, and this witness is in a position to provide further authentication for it, and we would like to tender it, Mr. President, as a document that came -- it's an HVO record captured at the fish farm, the HVO headquarters in Doljani at the end of July 1993. And clearly -- very clearly saying to Mico, Slavko, and Tuta, the European monitors and the Spanish Battalion are on their way. Now, we can argue about what that document means later. But the witness is in a position to say this is one of the documents that were found. And I don't know how it could have been any more transparent -- it does not relate to the diary. I've said that now several times.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Scott, after consultations with my colleagues, we believe that this document is relevant -- is irrelevant to the testimony of this witness, so you should not use this document for this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour. Thank you very much. I'll remember that for the rejoinder case as well. Thank you, witness. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, witness, I'm afraid that you have to stay in The Hague for another day, hopefully not over the weekend. And during your stay in The Hague, you are still under oath, so please do not talk to anybody about your testimony and do not let anybody talk to you about it. Do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I do, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Have a good rest. And we'll see you tomorrow morning at 9.30 in this courtroom. We are adjourned.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: be reconvened on Friday, the 11th day of October, 2002, at 9.00 a.m.
